CANONICAL_NAME.value: compact / uncompact (4.2BSD, 1983) -- adaptive Huffman file compression, the LOSER superseded by compress

value.lineage: Compression lineage, the SUPERSEDED DESIGN: compact (Colin McMaster, 1980; shipped in 4.xBSD ucb/) used Gallager's adaptive Huffman coding -- one-pass, no table transmitted, but slow and ~38% savings. compress (Thomas et al. 1984, LZW) beat it decisively on speed and ratio, then LZW's Unisys patent pressure produced gzip/DEFLATE (1992-93). Preserved from the unix-history-repo at tag BSD-4_2 (ucb/compact: compact.c, uncompact.c, tree.c, compact.h, Makefile, ccat.sh).

value.built_to: shrink files on 1980 disks with one pass and no side table, by adapting the Huffman tree as symbols arrive
value.pressure: disk scarcity; CPU cost; the arrival of LZW, which did better on both counts
value.success_means: round trip exact; the human record: the ratio and speed lost to compress within two years

value.pressure: storage scarcity, CPU cost, competition from a better algorithm
value.failure_condition: corrupt round trip; or -- historically -- being out-competed

evidence.ref: Welch, A Technique for High-Performance Data Compression, IEEE Computer 1984
evidence.says: LZW is presented as a fast, high-ratio compression technique; compress implemented it and became the standard Unix compressor, displacing the adaptive-Huffman compact.

evidence.ref: 4.xBSD distribution contents (compact in ucb/, later absent)
evidence.says: compact shipped in 4.xBSD and did not survive into later standard Unix toolsets.
